findings.criterion: AC3: every genuine live mirror has a linked ticket created `discovered_from` this task, proposing generate-or-gate using an existing repo pattern. Verified by `rebar deps f9b9-83ad-931c-4833` listing those links.
findings.detail: The ticket snapshot for f9b9-83ad-931c-4833 shows only one dep link in the `deps` array: `relates_to->c333-02f8-8e16-4cd8`. No `discovered_from` links from follow-up tickets are visible. The report (lines 325–334) asserts that 14 follow-up tickets were created and linked `discovered_from` this task, but the ticket snapshot I read contains no such links — no ticket IDs, link UUIDs, or other concrete specifics that would substantiate the claim. The criterion requires the links to be verifiable via `rebar deps`, and the snapshot shows they are not present (or not yet visible in the snapshot I read).
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment naming each of the 14 follow-up ticket IDs (with their link UUIDs or rebar dep output) that were created `discovered_from` f9b9-83ad-931c-4833, along with the timestamp when the links were created. If the links were created but are not yet visible in the ticket store snapshot, re-run `rebar deps f9b9-83ad-931c-4833` and paste the output as a comment.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
